PACKS.blurb: Seven days of trusting God with bills, budgets and the fear of not having enough.
days: God knows what I need before I even ask.
Matthew 6:8
What money worry is loudest today? Write it down and hand it to God.
I will not borrow worry from tomorrow; today has enough grace.
Matthew 6:34
List three needs that were met this week, big or small.
My God supplies every need I have.
Philippians 4:19
Where have you seen provision you didn’t plan for?
I can be content in plenty and in want, because Christ strengthens me.
Philippians 4:12-13
What would contentment look like in your budget this month?
I honour God with what I have, and He is faithful.
Proverbs 3:9-10
What is one small, generous step you could take this week?
I cast my cares on Him, because He cares for me.
1 Peter 5:7
Name the care you keep picking back up. What would it mean to leave it with Him?
I have never been forsaken, and I will not be now.
Psalm 37:25
Write a short prayer of trust for the month ahead.

PACKS.blurb: A gentle week for grieving hearts, with room to remember, mourn and hope.
days: The Lord is near to my broken heart.
Psalm 34:18
Write about a memory you want to keep close.
It is right for me to mourn, and I will be comforted.
Matthew 5:4
What do you miss most today?
God keeps every one of my tears; none are wasted.
Psalm 56:8
When did you last let yourself cry? What did it feel like?
Even in the valley of the shadow, He is with me.
Psalm 23:4
Where have you sensed God’s presence this week, even faintly?
My grief is real, and so is my hope.
1 Thessalonians 4:13-14
What would you say to them if you could?
Joy will come again in the morning.
Psalm 30:5
What small thing brought you comfort recently?
One day God will wipe away every tear.
Revelation 21:4
Write a prayer for the days ahead.

PACKS.blurb: Short, honest affirmations for long nights, small hands and a full heart.
days: God gently leads me as I care for my little one.
Isaiah 40:11
What is one moment from today you want to remember?
When I am tired, His strength is made perfect in my weakness.
2 Corinthians 12:9
Where do you need help right now? Who could you ask?
My child is fearfully and wonderfully made.
Psalm 139:14
Write a blessing over your child.
God comforts me the way a mother comforts her child.
Isaiah 66:13
How have you been comforted this week?
I can come to Jesus weary, and He gives me rest.
Matthew 11:28
What would rest look like for you this week, even for ten minutes?
His mercies are new for me every morning, even after a long night.
Lamentations 3:22-23
What grace did you need this morning?
My children are a gift from the Lord.
Psalm 127:3
Write a letter to your child about this season.

PACKS.blurb: For hard conversations, new roles and the quiet pressure of doing good work.
days: Whatever I do, I work at it with all my heart, as for the Lord.
Colossians 3:23
What is the hardest part of your work right now?
God has not given me a spirit of fear, but of power, love and a sound mind.
2 Timothy 1:7
Where is fear holding you back?
The Lord goes before me; I will not be afraid or dismayed.
Deuteronomy 31:8
What new step feels daunting? What would courage look like?
I commit my work to the Lord, and my plans are established.
Proverbs 16:3
Write down one plan and offer it to God.
I will not grow weary in doing good.
Galatians 6:9
Who at work could you encourage this week?
I work diligently and trust God with the outcome.
Proverbs 10:4
What are you proud of from this week?
I am God’s workmanship, created for good works.
Ephesians 2:10
What good work do you sense God calling you to?

SCAPES.s: A low, even hum for sleep

Keep gum or sugar-free mints with you today.

Wash the clothes and clean the car that hold the smell.
Swap your usual smoke break for a short walk.
Ask a doctor or pharmacist about quitting aids.
Work out how much money you’ve saved so far.
Install a content filter on your phone and laptop.
Keep devices out of the bedroom tonight.
Unfollow accounts that pull you toward temptation.
Choose an accountability partner and tell them today.
When tempted, leave the room and pray Psalm 51:10.
Set your phone to greyscale after 9 p.m.
Write who you want to be a year from now.
Block gambling sites and delete betting apps.
Ask your bank about blocking gambling transactions.
Let someone you trust hold your spare cash for a while.
List your debts or losses honestly, without judging yourself.
Plan what you’ll do during big games or events.
Look up a gambling support group near you.
Put the money you would have bet into savings.
Turn off all non-essential notifications.
Move social apps off your home screen.
Keep your phone in another room for the first hour of the day.
Set a time limit on your most-used app.
Replace one scroll session with reading a Psalm.
Charge your phone outside the bedroom.
Have one meal today with no screens.
Delete the contacts who supply you.
Remove any paraphernalia from your home.
Talk to a doctor about safe support for quitting.
Write down your highest-risk times and places.
Find a recovery meeting, in person or online.
Plan a sober activity for tonight.
Tell one trusted person about your goal.
Uninstall the game that takes the most time.
Set a hard stop for screens tonight.
Move consoles out of the bedroom.
Plan an offline activity with a friend.
Count how many hours you’ve won back this week.
Spend 30 minutes on an old hobby.
Turn off game notifications.

Anxious.note: When worry runs ahead of you, these words bring you back to now.

Weary.note: For the tired places, a strength that doesn’t depend on you.

Grieving.note: Grief and hope can sit side by side. Here is something to hold.

Lonely.note: You are seen and held, even when no one else is in the room.

Overwhelmed.note: One breath, one step, one promise at a time.

Uncertain.note: You don’t need the whole map. Here is light for the next step.

Hopeful.note: Lean into the hope you feel. It stands on firm ground.

TNOTE.Provision: God knows what you need, down to the last bill.
TNOTE.Healing: For your body and your heart, the Healer is near.
TNOTE.Peace: You can put the worry down for a moment. He is holding it.
TNOTE.Strength: You don’t have to be strong on your own today.
TNOTE.Wisdom: Ask freely. He gives wisdom without holding back.
TNOTE.Renewal: Mercy is bigger than the mistake.
TNOTE.Love: You are loved with a love that doesn’t leave.
TNOTE.Hope: Even here, hope has the last word.
TNOTE.Protection: You are covered, wherever you go today.
TNOTE.Faith: Small faith in a great God is enough.
TNOTE.Prayer: He hears you, every word and every silence.

JPROMPTS: What is one thing God showed you today?
Where did you feel peace today?
What are you anxious about? Write it as a prayer.
Who are you thankful for, and why?
What verse stayed with you this week?
Describe a moment from today you want to remember.
What do you need to forgive, or ask forgiveness for?
Where do you want to grow this month?
What answered prayer can you look back on?
If you had five quiet minutes with God, what would you say?
What is weighing on your heart tonight?
Write down three small joys from today.
What did you learn about yourself today?
Where did you see God’s kindness in someone else?
What are you hoping for right now?
What do you want to let go of before you sleep?

VAFF.2 Corinthians 12:9: His grace is enough for me today.

GEN_T: Read today’s verse aloud, slowly, twice.
Write down one trigger you noticed today.
Text or call someone who supports you.
Take a 15-minute walk without your phone.
Drink a full glass of water when a craving starts.
Pray for one other person who is struggling.
Write three things you’re thankful for.
Plan your evening, hour by hour.

Tell God honestly how today feels.

MDESC.1: The first day is often the hardest. You did it.
MDESC.14: Two weeks. New patterns are forming.
MDESC.90: Ninety days, a milestone many recovery programs celebrate.

SMOKE_HEALTH: Your heart rate and blood pressure drop.
The carbon monoxide level in your blood drops to normal.
Your circulation improves and your lung function increases.
Coughing and shortness of breath decrease.
Your risk of coronary heart disease is about half that of a smoker.
Your stroke risk can fall to that of a non-smoker.
Your risk of lung cancer falls to about half that of a smoker.
Your risk of coronary heart disease is that of a non-smoker.
SOS_PRAYER: Lord Jesus, You know this pull and You understand my weakness. I don’t want to go back. Give me Your strength for the next ten minutes, and the next. Thank You that there is no condemnation for me in You. Lead me in the way out You have promised. Amen.

AFFS.a: My faith is real today, and I trust God with what I cannot yet see.
I walk by faith and not by sight.
I pray with belief, and I trust God to answer.
My faith grows every time I take in God's word.
Even my small faith can move mountains.
All things are possible for me because I believe.
I bring every worry to God in prayer, with a thankful heart.
I call on God, and He shows me things I have not yet known.
My heart stays open to God throughout this day.
In my quiet place, my Father sees me and meets me.
My prayers matter, and they carry power.
I pray with confidence because God hears me.
I rest in the shelter of the Most High; He is my refuge and my fortress.
No weapon formed against me will prosper.
The Lord keeps me in my going out and in my coming in.
The Lord is faithful, and He guards me from evil.
The name of the Lord is my strong tower, and I am safe in it.
God has given His angels charge over me.
I receive the peace of Christ, and I will not let my heart be troubled.
My mind is fixed on God, so He keeps me in perfect peace.
God's peace guards my heart and my mind.
I lie down in peace and sleep, for the Lord keeps me safe.
I let the peace of God rule in my heart.
The Lord blesses me, keeps me, and gives me peace.
As I wait on the Lord, my strength is renewed.
I can do all things through Christ who strengthens me.
I am strong and courageous, for the Lord is with me wherever I go.
The Lord is my strength and my shield; my heart trusts in Him.
The joy of the Lord is my strength.
God's grace is enough for me, and His power is made perfect in my weakness.
Nothing can separate me from the love of God.
I love because God first loved me.
I am loved with an everlasting love.
The Lord my God is with me; He delights in me and sings over me.
I love others the way Christ has loved me.
Perfect love casts out my fear.
This is the day the Lord has made, and I will rejoice in it.
I give thanks in every circumstance.
I enter His gates with thanksgiving and His courts with praise.
I give thanks to the Lord, for He is good and His mercy endures forever.
Whatever I do, I do in Jesus' name, giving thanks to God.
His mercies are new to me every morning.
I trust the Lord with all my heart, and He directs my path.
I ask God for wisdom, and He gives it generously.
God's word is a lamp to my feet and a light to my path.
I commit my work to the Lord, and my plans are established.
I seek wisdom first, and I seek understanding with all I have.
The Lord gives me wisdom; knowledge and understanding come from Him.
Heal me, Lord, and I will be healed; save me, and I will be saved.
The Lord forgives me and heals me; I will not forget His benefits.
By His stripes I am healed.
The Lord heals my broken heart and binds up my wounds.
I listen to the Lord, for He is the Lord who heals me.
I prosper and am in health, even as my soul prospers.
My God supplies all my needs according to His riches in glory.
The Lord is my shepherd; I lack nothing.
I seek God's kingdom first, and everything I need is added to me.
Those who seek the Lord will not lack any good thing.
God is able to make all grace abound toward me.
I remember the Lord, who gives me the strength to work and provide.
The God of hope fills me with joy and peace as I trust Him.
God has plans for me, plans for peace and a future with hope.
God is working all things together for my good.
God is doing a new thing in my life.
I put my hope in God, and I will praise Him again.
I rejoice in hope, stay patient in trouble, and keep praying.
I confess my sins, and God is faithful to forgive and cleanse me.
God creates a clean heart in me and renews a right spirit within me.
In Christ I am a new creation; the old has passed away.
I forgive others as God in Christ has forgiven me.
My sins, though like scarlet, are made white as snow.
There is no condemnation for me in Christ Jesus.
